findings.title: CVE-2008-4128: Cisco IOS HTTP administration cross-site request forgery
findings.summary_md: The CVE record, published 2008-09-18, describes multiple cross-site request forgery vulnerabilities in the HTTP Administration component of Cisco IOS 12.4 on the 871 Integrated Services Router, allowing remote attackers to execute arbitrary commands via crafted requests to the /level/15/exec/- URIs. This is the 18-year-old bug the 2026 joint advisory names alongside CVE-2018-0171.

findings.title: CVE-2018-0171: Cisco IOS and IOS XE Smart Install remote code execution
findings.summary_md: Published 2018-03-28, the CVE record describes improper validation in the Smart Install feature of Cisco IOS and IOS XE that lets an unauthenticated remote attacker trigger a device reload (denial of service) or execute arbitrary code by sending crafted Smart Install packets. The feature is the core Cisco technology named in the 2026 Center 16 advisory.

findings.title: Cisco IOS and IOS XE Software Smart Install Remote Code Execution Vulnerability (cisco-sa-20180328-smi2)
findings.summary_md: Cisco's vendor advisory for CVE-2018-0171, dated March 28, 2018, covers the Smart Install remote code execution vulnerability in IOS and IOS XE and lists affected and fixed releases. Verified via its earliest Wayback snapshot from 2018-03-31; the page confirms the March 28, 2018 publication date.

findings.title: Iranian & Russian Networks Attacked Using Cisco's CVE-2018-0171 Vulnerability
findings.summary_md: In early April 2018, a group signing itself JHT mass-exploited CVE-2018-0171 (Smart Install) and overwrote device configurations on network infrastructure including Russian and Iranian networks. Iran's ICT ministry reported over 200,000 routers affected worldwide, with 3,500 in Iran. This is the earliest large-scale weaponization of the exact flaw the 2026 advisory says Center 16 still uses.

findings.title: Russian State-Sponsored Cyber Actors Targeting Network Infrastructure Devices (TA18-106A)
findings.summary_md: The joint FBI/DHS technical alert, released April 16, 2018, assessed that Russian state-sponsored actors exploited large numbers of enterprise and SOHO routers and switches worldwide, abusing GRE, SNMP (161/162), HTTP (80) and Cisco Smart Install (port 4786), and used compromised routers for man-in-the-middle attacks and persistent access. It advised hunting for TCP traffic to port 4786 from anything other than trusted management hosts and noted attackers harvest password hashes and SNMP community strings from stolen configuration files.

findings.title: Beers with Talos EP27: Smart Install, Vuln Process Realities, and Professional Wrestling
findings.summary_md: Cisco Talos' podcast episode, published April 20, 2018, discusses the Smart Install exploitation incident and the realities of the vulnerability disclosure process, weeks after CVE-2018-0171 was exploited in the wild. It documents the researcher-side response to the same exploitation wave the 2026 advisory revisits.
